brief: Syz's chart-pack wrap-up reports several parallel developments rather than one thesis. France's fiscal credibility deteriorated: the 10y OAT-Bund spread topped 100bps for the first time since 2012, yields near an 18-year high, 2026 deficit forecast at 5.4% of GDP versus a 5% target, and debt at 117% of GDP, with a 2027 target of 5% and a longer-run promise of 3% by 2029. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, hawkish and unanimous, with 16-of-18 dots pointing to another hike and markets pricing 89% odds of a December move; the 10y Treasury yield hit 5.04%, the highest since 2007. Separately, a Middle East supply shock (Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi's East-West pipeline) pushed Brent toward $110 and correlated oil with yields (WTI/10y correlation 0.96). AI stocks sold off early in the week on executive calls to slow development, then rebounded as investors judged an industry-wide pause unlikely given competition with China, with Nasdaq and Mag7 outperforming while breadth narrowed. The note reports these events; it does not argue a single connecting thesis between them.
